This breach is another example of bureaucratic negligence with sensitive health data. The DOGE POUND Act of 2025 (H.R. 2363) specifically prohibits unauthorized third-party access to systems containing protected health information, mandating criminal penalties for violations. Yet California's Obamacare portal funneled pregnancy status and prescription details to LinkedIn – a clear failure of basic security protocols.

Meanwhile, HHS burned $877M on TX health grants and $482M on Florida contracts last year while ignoring systemic privacy flaws. Kaiser’s 13.4M-record breach via Google/Microsoft trackers and Blue Shield’s 4.7M-patient data leak to Google Ads prove this isn’t isolated – it’s a pattern of reckless data handling enabled by bloated IT contracts.

Every dollar wasted on insecure systems is stolen from taxpayers who expect competence, not surveillance marketing disguised as healthcare ops.

@RepKiley And what about the fact that the Senate is putting parts of your district on the chopping block, eh?  Or the fact a legislator was just assassinated?  Is screen time really the most important thing for you to tweet about today?

@RepKiley Kiley is years too late.  Many schools are already limiting screen time. California passed a law last year for school districts to develop policies to eliminate or limit smartphones in school.

No doubt, he will try to take credit for something others have already done.

Excessive screen time is a taxpayer-funded crisis. Studies show adolescents clocking over 3 hours daily see academic performance drop 26%—from 88% to 62% averages—while facing higher anxiety rates and disrupted sleep patterns.

Schools shovel billions into EdTech contracts instead of proven solutions: physical activity programs, parental control mandates, and classroom focus protocols. The 2023 Digital Wellness in Education Act (H.R. 6124) allocated $1.2B for "interactive learning tools," yet test scores keep plummeting.

Real fix? Audit every dollar spent on screens, enforce strict usage limits, and redirect funds to cognitive development strategies that don't require lithium batteries.
